content.main_title: What Is My ISP - Internet Service Provider Lookup Tool
content.main_desc: Instantly identify your Internet Service Provider (ISP), organization name, network details, and connection information. Our free ISP lookup tool reveals your ISP name, ASN (Autonomous System Number), IP address, location, and network infrastructure. Perfect for verifying VPN connections, troubleshooting network issues, confirming business internet lines, and understanding your network routing.
content.info1: ISP Name: The company providing your internet connection
content.info2: Organization: The organization or entity managing your network connection
content.info3: ASN: Unique network identifier for routing and peering
content.info4: Location: City, region, and country associated with your connection
content.info5: Network Details: IP range, subnet information, and network infrastructure data

content.asn_desc: An Autonomous System Number (ASN) is a globally unique identifier assigned to a network or group of networks under a single administrative control. ISPs, large organizations, and content delivery networks each have their own ASN. This number is used in BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) routing to determine how internet traffic flows between different networks. Knowing your ASN helps identify your network provider and understand routing paths.

content.isp_type2: Cable ISPs: High-speed internet via coaxial cable infrastructure
content.isp_type3: Fiber Optic ISPs: Ultra-fast connections using fiber optic cables
content.isp_type5: Satellite ISPs: Internet via satellite for remote areas
content.isp_type6: Business ISPs: Dedicated enterprise-grade connections with SLAs
content.privacy_note_desc: Your ISP can see all unencrypted internet traffic and the websites you visit (but not HTTPS content). They may log connection data, browsing history, and DNS queries. Use a VPN to encrypt your traffic and prevent ISP monitoring. Our tool only displays publicly available information that websites can already see.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.a1: ISP stands for Internet Service Provider - the company that provides your internet connection. Examples include Comcast, AT&T, Verizon, or local providers. Your ISP assigns your IP address and routes all your internet traffic.
faq.a2: ASN (Autonomous System Number) is a unique identifier assigned to networks and ISPs for internet routing. It helps identify which organization controls a block of IP addresses. Large ISPs have their own ASN, while smaller providers may share one.
faq.q3: Can I hide my ISP information?
faq.a3: Using a VPN (Virtual Private Network) will show the VPN provider's ISP instead of your actual ISP. However, your real ISP can still see that you're using a VPN. Proxies and Tor can also mask your ISP information.
